svg.font-family: Arial, Noto Sans CJK SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif
svg.title: Failure recovery: candidates, pages, partial commits, durable success
svg.desc: Shows recovery behavior across four failure positions: A. Uncommitted candidate or pre-decision failure restores intact span; B. Paused backend continuation saves accepted pages and ledger while main history stays unchanged; C. Multi-chunk partial commit keeps earlier committed chunks; D. Post-decision live publication failure quarantines writer and requires cold reopen.
svg.text: Failure recovery: candidates, pages, partial commits, durable success
A. Current span has not reached durable success

text.tspan: • Timeout, rejected candidate, archive error,
or failure before the durable success decision.
• Discard candidate, or attempt verified backup restore.
If restore fails, quarantine and retain recovery data.
• Report known attempts; missing usage stays unknown.

svg.text: B. Continuation interrupted or budget exhausted

text.tspan: • A page fails or the finite call budget is exhausted.
• Accepted pages saved ≠ main history replaced.
• Preserve source identity, accepted pages, and usage.
New /compact can renew an exhausted finite allowance.
• Source edits may require redo; earlier chunks can remain.

svg.text: C. Later chunk fails after earlier commits

text.tspan: • Earlier chunks commit; a later chunk fails.
• Each accepted chunk is committed independently.
Preserve the successfully committed checkpoints.
• Only uncommitted spans keep original visible messages.
• Missing request usage remains unknown.

svg.text: D. Publication failure after durable success

text.tspan: • Replacement and success decision are durable,
then publication to the live in-memory session fails.
• Quarantine the writer; preserve committed disk history.
Reopen the session from its durable log.
• Recovery must verify evidence before allowing work.
